items.question: When a practice is not stated in Siddhānta, may one take the Garuda and other agamas as authority?
premises: Siddhānta may not state every practice.
Garuda and other agamas can supply missing authority.
The verse directs acceptance when Siddhānta is silent.
items.inference: Silence in Siddhānta permits recourse to Garuda and related agamas.
uncertainties: Exact scope of gāruḍa+ādyaṃ remains unclear.
items.plain_english: If something is not stated in the Siddhānta, then the Garuda and other texts should be taken up.
